criteria.criterion: A new Markdown file under docs/design/ exists in the diff and describes landing each job as one commit in one pull request cut from current main, instead of stacking on a long-lived local branch.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. It creates docs/design/per-job-landing-branches.md. Section 1 describes today's stacked local branch. Section 2 describes the new design: cut each job's commit from current main with merge_tree and commit_tree (one parent, main), use one branch per job via work_branch(job), and keep exactly one commit per pull request.

criteria.criterion: The note cites throughput review 20261108-183648-5eya and the measured figures 1537.1 of 1582.1 median minutes (THROUGHPUT.md), checkable by Grep for the review id in the new file.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The review id appears in the Source line and in sections 1, 5, 8 and 10. Section 1 cites '1537.1 of the 1582.1-minute median' as measured, from the review and THROUGHPUT.md. I compared it with the evidence record records/throughput-reviews/2026-11/20261108-183648-5eya.json: landings 414, window_median_minutes 1582.15, expected_minutes_saved 1530.0. All match the note.

criteria.criterion: The note states the predicted saving (1530.0 minutes per landed job) labeled as an estimate, and says how the next throughput review measures the minutes after the change landed.
criteria.evidence: Section 5 labels the 1530.0-minute saving per landed job a prediction, 'an estimate and not a measurement'. It also says how the next review measures it: THROUGHPUT_WINDOW (20) with StageMinutes::median_of, the total compared with 1582.1, the stage compared with 1537.1, and the saving set against 1530.0. Only landings after the change count, and the number of commits per pull request decides whether the drop is credited to this change. I confirmed THROUGHPUT_WINDOW = 20 and median_of exist in crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs.

criteria.criterion: The note has an Existing code section that reuses or extends docs/design/continuous-landing.md, docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md and crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs, naming what is kept and what changes.
criteria.evidence: Section 3 is a table marking each item Kept or Changed. It covers the Git primitives in athena-git/src/lib.rs, continuous-landing.md (D155) and squash-chain-landing.md. I grepped for every cited function: merge_tree, commit_tree, commit_with_records, push_branch, fetch_remote_branch, is_ancestor, replay (at line 828 as stated), plan_rebase, Rebase, rebase_job_branch, records_only_message, land_pr, resync_onto_merge, resync_tip, rebase_needs_recheck, recheck_after_rebase and the land_pr_refuses... test. All exist where the note says.

criteria.criterion: The note lists alternatives considered (for example keep stacking with squash, rebase the stack) with reasons for rejection, and the risks such as conflicts and landing order when cutting from main.
criteria.evidence: Section 6 lists seven alternatives, each with a reason, including keep stacking with squash, rebase the stack more often, chained pull requests and cherry-pick. Section 7 lists risks, including conflicts with main, landing order and dependency on an unlanded job, drift in verified content, main moving while the pull request waits, interaction with continuous landing, existing stacked branches, and a misread saving.

criteria.criterion: The diff touches only files under docs/design/ (git diff --stat), and contains no secrets or personal data.
criteria.evidence: git diff HEAD~1 --stat lists three files, all under docs/design/. I read the diff and found no credentials, tokens or email addresses.

findings.summary: CHANGELOG.md is an expected deliverable and the changelog default applies, but the change does not modify it.
findings.evidence: The deliverables list says 'CHANGELOG.md (modify)', and the changelog default says the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md. git diff HEAD~1 --stat shows only the three docs/design/ files. Earlier design-only notes have entries, such as CHANGELOG.md line 490 for continuous-landing.md (D155) and line 497 for warm-baseline-build.md, so this one should too.

findings.summary: The note says the stage is defined in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, but StageMinutes is defined in crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs.
findings.evidence: Grep shows 'pub struct StageMinutes' at crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs:102. status.rs only uses it in tests. Section 8 ('the stage definition in status.rs') has the same imprecision.

findings.summary: The attribution rule is weak if continuous landing ships in the same window.
findings.evidence: Section 5 credits a drop to this change if every landed pull request holds one commit. That shows the design was in force, but it does not separate this saving from a saving made by continuous-landing.md in the same window. The per-phase split from build job 1 is the stronger measure, and the note could say the review uses it.

summary: The design note docs/design/per-job-landing-branches.md does what the request asked, and all six acceptance criteria are met. The verdict is still fail, because CHANGELOG.md was not updated. It is on the expected deliverables list, the changelog default applies, and earlier design notes have changelog entries (for example continuous-landing.md and warm-baseline-build.md), so its absence is a major finding. The note describes cutting each job's commit from current main, one commit per pull request, and explains how that removes the stacked re-carrying of earlier commits. It cites review 20261108-183648-5eya and the 1537.1 of 1582.1 median minutes, which match the review record in the evidence snapshot. It labels the 1530.0-minute saving an estimate and explains how the next review measures it. Its Existing code table, alternatives and risks all match the code: every function, test and line number it cites exists where it says. The approach is sound. Two minor points: the file path given for StageMinutes is imprecise, and the attribution rule would be stronger if it used the per-phase split from build job 1.
